According to the rules for voting on Reddit, downvotes should only be used for content that doesn't add to the discussion, not to indicate disagreement. However, as we all know, this is not the case today. Despite the efforts of many, users continue to use downvotes as a tool to reduce the visibility of disagreeable content.

I have not seen many (if any at all) downvotes to indicate disagreement on this site so far. However, it is inevitable as our user base grows that this will become a problem. The severity of the problem is debatable.

What should we do about this? Do we want to enforce the previous guidelines for voting? Or do we want to embrace the opinion-based voting system? If we don't want downvotes to indicate disagreement, how can we make sure that they are not abused? If we do allow for the opinion-based voting, how can we ensure that everyone with a valid, constructive comment has visibility?

A possible suggestion that I have would be to make upvotes the only factor for which comments rise to the top in the discussion sections (unless maybe the net karma count is negative). Maybe then there could be a flag button that sends flagged comments to the bottom of the thread. There would need to be some assurance that the flag system would not be abused though.

Just some thoughts. Does anyone else have any ideas?
The Opinion Voting System: Suggestions for change

If you want to catch downvotes here, just make a suggestion for the site that would hinder power users. After that, they'll go out of their way to downvote almost any comment you make.Then, they'll proceed to call you a shill, whine about how this site is in it's "infancy," and finally argue with zero logic. What people don't get is that everything that's being implemented can easily be reversed if the majority don't like it (given that it's not going to leave the site vulnerable). We haven't even gotten to closed beta, yet.

Now, if I personally used the downvote system for articles, it would only be used for sites that were posted that have a history of buzz word abuse, misleading headlines, and click baits. If the headline is "New discovery prevents HIV" but in the article it says, "which could be used to help prevent HIV, but further study is needed" then I will definitely give a downvote. And unfortunately, there have been articles posted on here that have that.

Going off of your flagging idea, who would be the one to allow or disallow the flag to go through? If the moderator, what makes you think that the moderator that decides is competent enough to make that assessment? I made a post regarding WhoaVerse in Technology, and a mod said it wasn't tech related. Of course it's tech related. The internet is technology. Incompetency at it's finest.

Now, if the flagging system went off of how many members flagged it, then that might work. Of course, anyone can create an account within seconds, so they could push their agenda to flag anything multiple times. Given an hour, someone could flag a lot into oblivion. As extreme as this might sound, it really does put it into perspective. Of course, the person doing that would go after every post/comment this person has made and continue flagging them until they rage quit the entire site.

tl;dr People downvote the people they don't like, flagging could easily be abused, and I can't think of anything that would work better than the current system. Aside from a downvote limiter, there isn't much that can be done. That is, of course, my opinion.

You sound like you got "the business" over on Reddit. As someone who has also gotten "the business" (I rebuffed the advances of some crazy Aussie power-user) I'd like to offer my condolences, and some simple advice to you or any other reader in escaping such an awful situation. Create a new account.

This doesn't mean you'll be leaving all those yummy imaginary fake internet points behind forever, just for a few months. That power-user has to manually go look for your comments or submissions to go downvote (and I pity any soul who feels the need to waste time doing such a thing), and if they feel you have left, they'll get bored and stop. You can always go back to your old account later (I waited 6 months). Anyways, it worked for me.

I haven't had a reddit account in years. As for here, I'm not going to create a new account because I don't care if someone continuously comes after me. Let them. I'm not worried, it's not a safety concern, and it is only the internet.

I'm for keeping it real. They're about opinions. That's how everyone uses them and sees them, regardless of what you tell people it's for. You can tell people to only upvote when someone spells everything correctly, advocates world peace or whatever and you will still get people who upvote something that like or agree with and downvotes something they don't like.
